digest.component_or_area: plan-review gate: context-limit escalation and model ladder sizing
propositions: For a non-Anthropic-family primary (e.g., bedrock:us.amazon.nova-pro-v1:0), models_at_or_above fails to locate the starting rung in MODEL_LADDER and falls through to returning the entire ladder, causing escalation to downgrade to claude-haiku-4-5 and cross provider families.

largest_window_tokens returns MODEL_LADDER[-1][1] (1000000) for an unlocated primary instead of a conservative estimate, causing P8 to under-block and permit truncation instead of emitting a too-big finding.

Pass-1 escalation assigns the first returned model directly to the run config (replace(cfg, model=model)), so an unlocated primary escalates to a smaller window and different provider on the first attempt.

prerequisite-coverage escalation at prerequisites.py:260-261 has the same defect: it calls models_at_or_above(model) then takes ladder[0], causing an IndexError that is converted to input-too-large only by accident.

The fix must return [model] (not []) from models_at_or_above for a truthy-but-unlocated primary to preserve the single-criterion retry before escalation, and return ladder minimum (not maximum) from largest_window_tokens to enforce conservative blocking.

Three assertions in tests/unit/test_model_class_ladder.py pin the defective behaviour (models_at_or_above(some-unknown-model) returning full ladder, largest_window_tokens returning 1000000 for nova) and must be updated when the fix lands.
